models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Light northerlies and a flat sea over the Aeolians now - but the forecast ends 3 Oct, a day before we sail.
briefing.synopsis: Current pattern is a slack, weakly gradient northerly regime: across all six islands the consensus shows N-NNE winds easing from 6-10 kt on 27 Sep (Stromboli highest at 9.8 kt, gusting 20.0 kt at midnight) to 1-5 kt by 29 Sep, with directions wandering as the gradient collapses. Seas fall with it - total wave 1.7-2.1 ft today down to 0.1-0.5 ft by the 29th on ECMWF IFS/AIFS (both 27 Sep 06Z) and ICON-2i (27 Sep 12Z), with MFWAM (27 Sep 00Z) and ECMWF WAM in agreement on the decay. If this pattern held into the trip it would mean motoring more than sailing, flat water, and no shelter constraints at any of the planned berths. That is a big if: the models only reach 3 Oct 23:00 and we depart on the 4th, so nothing here is a forecast for the trip dates.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: No fleet berth tonight - the boats are not yet in the water. For reference, Portorosa Marina is the recommended base and scores as fully sheltered (enclosed marina, all-round shelter); the only forecast berth night inside the horizon, 3 Oct, shows SSE 3.5 kt gusting 11.7 kt with 0.3 ft NNW swell there. Nothing in the payload would push a boat off that berth.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Tomorrow (28 Sep) is nine days of pattern ahead of us, not a departure day. For the record, the models split on Portorosa overnight and midday: 0.9-7.0 kt at 00:00 and 1.8-8.2 kt at 12:00, a spread wide enough that the mean is not meaningful - elsewhere the islands hold 1-4 kt. The first real departure window, Portorosa to Lipari on 4 Oct, is beyond the forecast horizon of 3 Oct 23:00 and I have no data for it; expect the first usable numbers about three days before the start.

No forecast. Rehearsal on 1 Oct: 3.7 kt on a run.

cautions: Every trip date is outside the model horizon (forecast reaches 3 Oct 23:00; we depart 4 Oct). The 'go' verdicts in the rehearsal are scored against this week's live weather, not the trip - treat them as a check on the analysis, not a plan.
Portorosa 28 Sep shows genuine model disagreement: 0.9-7.0 kt at 00:00 and 1.8-8.2 kt at 12:00. Stromboli 28 Sep 06:00 spans 0.0-7.2 kt. Quote the range, not a mean.

Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli scores only 'workable' even in this calm spell - it is open from every direction and depends entirely on the sea staying down. Keep it under review when real numbers arrive.
ICON-2i runs only ~60-72 h ahead, so the finest-grid opinion will not cover the trip until we are almost alongside it.
briefing.confidence_note: The synoptic read on this week is well supported - stability tracking shows mean wind shifts under 1.1 kt at every lead time - but direction shifts average 60 degrees at 72-120 h and the trip dates sit entirely beyond the 3 Oct forecast horizon, so confidence for the voyage itself is low by definition.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
